ledger.note: The Cantabri of the northern Spanish mountains. The page gives no founding: 'a Cantabrian mercenary contingent is mentioned in Hannibal's army' and Cantabrian bands fought for the Vaccaei and Celtiberians 'in the Celtiberian Wars of the 2nd century BC'. 200 is a placeholder (page silent).

region.text: 'much of the highlands of the northern Spanish Atlantic coast', 'the whole of modern Cantabria province', eastern Asturias and parts of Palencia, Burgos and León; the disc cuts the provinces to the mountain country

ledger.note: 29 BC: the Cantabrian Wars begin. 'The Cantabrian Wars (29-19 BC)' are 'the final stage of Rome's conquest of Hispania'; the Cantabri page: 'backing of a Vaccaei anti-Roman revolt in 29 BC'. Augustus moved to Segisama in 26 BC 'to supervise the campaign in person'; the Astures were beaten at Lancia and Mons Medullius in 25.

ledger.note: 19 BC: 'The major fighting was completed in 19 BC.' The Cantabri page: 'conquest and partial annihilation by Emperor Augustus'; 'a serious slave revolt in 20 BC' spread to Asturias, and minor rebellions lasted until 16 BC.

zones.text: 'much of the highlands of the northern Spanish Atlantic coast', 'the whole of modern Cantabria province', eastern Asturias and parts of Palencia, Burgos and León; the disc cuts the provinces to the mountain country

wars.outcome: Roman victory under Augustus and Agrippa: Cantabria, Asturias and Gallaecia came under Roman control as part of Hispania; the Cantabri were largely annihilated.
wars.note: '29-19 BC'; Augustus at Segisama in 26; Carisius against the Astures in 25; minor rebellions to 16 BC. The Cantabri page gives no span for the war and credits Agrippa's harsh measures without a year.

certainty.note: Mountain country with tribal limits; no boundary line is given by either page.

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria. Thin: the tribes were a loose group; the disc used to cut Palencia, Burgos and Leon to the mountain country is the researcher's, since the page says only 'parts of Castile and Leon'. The Astures and Gallaeci (also in the wars page) have no dossier. The counterpart is roman-empire because the wars fall after Actium (31 BC) and Cliopatria's Roman Empire begins in -31; roman-republic's dossier ends in 30. Start 200 is a placeholder. Wikidata id left null. Family 'iberia' is a registry key.
